description.text: The enoyl-CoA hydratase/isomerase family comprises enzymes involved in fatty acid metabolism and benzoyl-CoA catabolism. Members of this family catalyze the hydration of double bonds in enoyl-CoA intermediates, a critical step in the beta-oxidation pathway. Some enzymes in this family also participate in the breakdown of alicyclic compounds, such as the conversion of 6-oxocyclohex-1-ene-1-carbonyl-CoA to 3-hydroxypimelyl-CoA, which is part of the benzoyl-CoA degradation route. The family's broad substrate range includes straight-chain enoyl-CoA thioesters from C4 to at least C16. The enzymes are characterized by their ability to facilitate the isomerization or hydration of unsaturated acyl-CoAs, playing a pivotal role in lipid metabolism and energy production.
